summary: Plan 06 P6.4 to P6.6 are delivered as CP07c-prep and CP07c, each as an exact-candidate authorization pull request followed by its consuming change pull request. The generic Architecture Conformance engine takes its final V3 location docs/guards/V3/stages/post/gates/architecture/dotnet, with the project and assembly named Guards.ArchitectureConformance; the C# namespace stays LayerGuard as an internal compatibility surface, not a stable gate identity, so the base-owned engine tests keep compiling across the move. CP07c-prep is the expand step: it creates the final V3 project and test paths while the engine sources are still in V3_ifx, so the same base-owned assertions run before and after the move. The V3 engine project forwards to the V3_ifx engine for this one checkpoint, the engine tests and their synthetic fixtures move to their final V3 paths and reference only the V3 engine project, the old V3_ifx test project stays declared but empty because candidate verification restores the previous base's engine tests there, and base-owned ownership moves to the V3 paths so that CP07c's candidate verification restores tests that compile against the moved engine. The IFX policy binding tests get their own minimal IFX fixture in V3_ifx and depend on no engine test data. CP07c then moves the engine sources into the V3 project, deletes the V3_ifx engine project and the empty test project, points the IFX binding and host at the V3 project, writes the hybrid trust contract of section 11.3 including the MSBuild import and Condition blind spots and their cross cover with the Assembly checks, and proves that the composite policy hash, the report fields, the failure categories and the v3-architecture check name are unchanged.
rationale: Section 8.2 step 3 puts the generic engine in V3 and leaves V3_ifx with policy, baseline, binding and IFX fixtures. Placing it at the final stage path now avoids a second protected move during the physical migration of P10. Renaming the C# namespace was rejected for this checkpoint because candidate verification compiles the previous base's engine tests against the candidate, and a namespace rename would break them; the stable identity Plan 06 protects is the gate and check name, and the project and assembly already carry the new name. The bridge is required because the base-owned test project reference is itself part of what the overlay restores: without a stable V3 project path that already exists before the move, the restored tests would reference a project that the move deletes, and ignoring them would defeat base-owned validation. The empty V3_ifx test project exists only so the restored previous-base tests still compile and run during CP07c-prep's own verification; CP07c deletes it once the base no longer owns that path. The user approved the V3 stage path, the project and assembly rename with the namespace kept as an internal compatibility surface, the IFX-specific fixture and the explicit bridge on 2026-09-18. Refines D12 and D27.
